items.title: NEW — `Style`'s CONDITION MODEL is the source of the styling pain: a condition is a COMBINATOR WRAPPING an inner style (`hover(inner)`, `attribute(name, value, inner)`), one condition per axis slot, nested outside-in in a fixed order — so two pseudo-classes on one rule are unspellable (`hover:not(:active)` becomes a raw token that miscompiles when wrapped, B311), `not` had to be a MARKER read by the enclosing combinator (A89), the author memorises `md(within(attribute(hover(..))))` or meets a refusal, and every wrap mints an intermediate style whose rules land dead on the sheet (B308). REDESIGN: a condition is a VALUE — `hover()`, `active().not()`, `pseudo("focus-visible")`, `attribute("disabled")` (presence), `attribute("data-selected").eq("true")`, `within(..)`, `children()`, `md()` — a rule is `style()…on(conditions..)`, rules compose by `.add(rule)` (an inner rule inherits the outer's conditions), and the compiler CANONICALISES the set into the slot order (media, relation, attributes, pseudos): duplicates merge, only a contradiction (`hover()` with `hover().not()`) refuses; `.hover(inner)` and friends stay as one-condition sugar; the css block's name-blind head takes the arguments it already parses as expressions (`.on(hover(), active().not()) { … }`; `.hover { }` = `.on(hover()) { }`), no bare selectors. B308 dies structurally (a rule set is a value, emitted once at application), B311 and the two-pseudo gap die (no condition is ever a string), A89's marker and A93's fence go, `Style::when`'s runtime merge becomes const `.add` composition. BREAKING for every `hover(inner)` in std, kolt, the website and the docs — a mechanical migration. L; a PAPER before any lane: canonicalisation and the specificity band (ui-styling §0bis) are where a hasty version goes wrong
items.discussion: the owner's critique and sketch (2026-09-12): `style().set("outline-offset", Length::zero()).add(style().color(Color::blue(500)).pseudo(pseudo("hover")).pseudo(pseudo("active").not()).attribute(attribute("disabled").not()))`, and in block form `css { outline-offset: 0; .add {} }`; kolt's `new_button_style` (styles.vl:62–86, rewritten 2026-09-12) is the exhibit — four gates forced into raw pseudo tokens; my refinement (accepted for the paper's starting point): one `.on(..)` taking the condition set, typed condition values with `.not()`/`.eq()`, canonicalisation in place of the nesting-order refusals. Paper on the next order, RULED before any build
items.body:
**The model.** A `Style` = base declarations + a set of RULES; a rule = a CONDITION SET + declarations. `style().color(c).on(hover(), active().not(), attribute("disabled").not())` is one rule; `outer.add(inner)` nests: `inner`'s rules carry `outer`'s conditions too, `inner`'s base declarations become a rule under `outer`'s conditions, and an `.add` with no conditions on either side is today's merge (`+`). Condition values are typed (`Pseudo`, `Attribute`, `Relation`, `Media`), `.not()` is a method on each, `attribute(name)` is presence and `.eq(value)` the valued form (A89's `Option<str>` argument folds into it); `pseudo(name)` keeps its leading-`!` fence and REFUSES a `:` in the name (the token is one pseudo-class; two are two values — B311's whole class becomes unspellable).

**Canonicalisation.** The set sorts into the shipped slot order (media, relation, attributes, pseudos — the sheet's band is still the OUTERMOST kind, so ui-styling §0bis's specificity story survives unchanged); equal conditions merge; a value and its negation refuse at const time (curated, one row). The nesting-order refusals (`.dark { .md { } }` out of order, one-pseudo-per-slot) go away because there is no nesting order to get wrong.

**What stays.** `hover(inner)`/`md(inner)`/`attribute(name, value, inner)` as sugar for `.add(inner.on(..))` so the estate migrates mechanically (or is rewritten by the E167 converter); `when(condition, delta)` (A36) for RUNTIME conditions; `Declarations`/`rule`/`declare` ride the same values; `raw`; the class-list emission and the split gate.

**What it closes.** B308 (no intermediate styles exist to emit dead rules — a rule set is a value until `class_list`/application); B311 (`pseudo_not` is never needed); A89's marker mechanism (replaced, its pins rewritten); A93 (`children()`/`divide()` are relation values, `child_relation`'s raw hatch is deleted). Order 30's compact-styling measurement (css-block §15.3) is re-run after: the const class list should not move.

**The block spelling.** `.on(hover(), active().not()) { color: {c}; }` — the head is already an expression list the lowering passes through name-blind (`css.rs`), so no grammar change; `.hover { }` stays as `.on(hover()) { }`. The owner's `.add {}` with no head is a plain nested merge = flatten into the parent, which the formatter can offer as a fix. No bare selectors (css-block.md §10's refusal stands).

**Owner's sketch, and the two places I diverge.** (1) `.pseudo(pseudo("hover"))` doubles the word — `.on(hover())` names the axis once; (2) `.set(property, Length)` — a typed `raw`, which is css-block §6's S1 groundwork (typed values in `raw`) and is taken as-is.

**Cost.** style.vl's condition machinery (~1400 lines around the combinators) rewritten on condition sets; the formatter's `STYLE_CONDITION_METHODS`/`ConditionAxis` sort becomes a canonicaliser; completion tables (css-block §7.1) and `style_table_sync` follow; guide + reference pages rewritten; kolt/website/docs migrate (mechanical). Paper questions: the canonical order of pseudos within the slot (written order vs. a fixed table), whether `.on` on a style that already has rules applies to the rules too (yes: conditions are intersected), and whether `hover(inner)` sugar is kept or deleted at the migration.

items.title: NEW — the shipped "Convert to a `css` block" refactor (css-block S5, `Document::css_spelling_conversion`) never fires on real code: the seed must be a BARE `style()` (`style_chain_links` matches `Node::Accessor("style")` only, so `style::style()` — the web prelude's own spelling, the one the templates and kolt write — is refused), and any TYPED link (`.color(c)`, `.flex_row()`, `.padding_x(..)`: every shorthand, i.e. every link an app writes) returns `None` for the WHOLE chain, because `render_css_items` knows only `raw` and the condition table. Make it fire: accept a path seed ending in `style()`; render a typed link as the declarations its std body writes — `STYLE_PROPERTY_METHODS.properties` names them and style.vl's bodies are `with_length`/`with_color`/`raw` chains, so inlining the body with the argument as a hole is exact (`padding_x(v)` → `padding-left: {v}; padding-right: {v};`, `flex_row()` → its two literals); a link with no block spelling (`when`, `add`, `rule`, `class_list`, a user extension such as kolt's `select_off`) becomes a TRAILING CHAIN on the block — `css { … }.select_off()` parses and types today (probed 2026-09-12) — instead of refusing the conversion
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-12): a quick fix that turns a style chain into a css block — it has existed as a `refactor.rewrite` action since css-block S5 and cannot appear on a single chain in kolt, for the two reasons above; both are in the converter's own doc comments ('the seed is a bare `style()` call', 'not a row of the lowering table … not this refactor's to invent'). A95's redesign changes the condition rows, not this mechanism
items.body:
**Seed.** `style_chain_links` accepts a `Node::Path`/member path whose last segment is `style` called with no arguments (`style::style()`, `s::style()`); the program is available to the code-action path when one is wanted for resolving the alias, but the raw-parse rule (last segment `style`, zero arguments) matches every spelling in the estate.

**Typed links.** Two sources, and the choice is the design point: (a) a hand table beside `STYLE_PROPERTY_METHODS` giving each method's declarations with `$1`/`$2` holes for its arguments, gated by `style_table_sync.rs` against style.vl's bodies exactly as the `family` column is; (b) an INLINER over std's parsed `style.vl`: a shorthand body is a chain of `with_length(prop, value)`/`with_color`/`raw(prop, literal)` links over `self`, so substituting the call's argument text into the parameter's holes yields the declarations with no second table. Recommendation: (b) — it cannot drift, and a body that is not such a chain (a barrier) simply has no block spelling. Values render through `render_block_value`'s existing rule: a string literal token run as itself, anything else as a hole `{expr}`; a `Length`/`Color` argument is a hole (`gap: {Length::rem(0.5)};`), a numeric literal too.

**Unconvertible links.** Today one such link refuses the whole chain. New rule: split the chain at the first link with no block spelling; everything before it becomes the block, the rest is written as a postfix chain on the block (`css { … }.when(selected, delta).class_list()`); condition combinators keep converting recursively as they do. A link BEFORE a convertible one that has no spelling (e.g. `.raw("outline", i"..")` is fine, but `.add(other)` in the middle) — the split is at the FIRST such link, so `style().color(c).add(x).gap(g)` becomes `css { color: {c}; }.add(x).gap(g)`, which is equal (chain order is merge order and the tail keeps it).

**Round trip.** A typed chain → block → chain lands on `raw` links, not the shorthands; that is the block's meaning (§5.2) and is documented rather than fought. Comments still refuse (unchanged).

**Pins.** the `style::style()` seed; kolt's `new_button_style` shape (typed links + raw + attribute/pseudo combinators) converts and the converted block's `class_list()` equals the chain's (the corpus twin proves the block == chain equivalence already); a chain with a user extension splits at the extension; a chain of only unconvertible links offers nothing; `book_sync`'s title gate unchanged (no new titles). Docs: the editor page's refactor row gains the sentence about the trailing chain.
